activity_context.topic_title: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums

feedback.problem: What is ${\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{arctan}⁡x\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
feedback.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{arctan}⁡x\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,$ the lower bound is $a=0,$ and the upper bound is $b=1.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{1-0}{n}=\frac{1}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{arctan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(0+i\cdot \frac{1}{n})\,\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(\frac{i}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{i}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
